title: Rabbi Yaakov ben Dostai (Dasi, Dasai, Dosai)

paragraphs: Rabbi Yaakov ben Dostai. Dasi — Dasai — Dosai.

In [Ketubot 111b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.111b.23), Rabbi Yaakov ben Dostai says: "From Lod to Ono is three mil; I started out early at twilight and walked up to my ankles in fig honey" (and the reading of [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2129&lang=en) is "ben Dosai"). And in [Yerushalmi Shabbat ch. 7 halakhah 1 (25a)](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.1.10) and [Bava Batra ch. 2 halakhah 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Batra.2.9.2) he is mentioned under the name Rabbi Yaakov ben Dosai; in [Makkot ch. 1 halakhah 7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Makkot.1.7.2) under the name Rabbi Yaakov bar Dasi; and in [Sanhedrin beginning of ch. 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.4.1.6) under the name Rabbi Yaakov bar Dasayi.

And in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, printed in Seder HaChachamim part 1, ch. 4, item 21, it says that Rabbi Yaakov ben Dosai was in the time of Rabbi Meir, and Hyman calls this a scribal error. The error came from [Yerushalmi Sanhedrin ch. 2, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.2.1.5), which says there: Rabbi Yaakov ben Dasai discusses the point of difference between them — Rabbi Meir used to say ... Rabbi Yehudah says ... . But Hyman takes the plain meaning to be that Rabbi Yaakov ben Dosai was explaining that whether one interrupts [the Temple service] is the point of difference between them, as [Pnei Moshe](https://www.sefaria.org/Penei_Moshe_on_Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.2.1.5.5) explains there.

notes.text: The Bavli passage is on 111b, though Hyman’s Hebrew cites 111a. The Bavli says ankle-deep, while Heilprin’s linked notice says shoulder-deep. Neshef means twilight and leaves morning or evening open.

Pnei Moshe explains the point of difference as whether the high priest interrupts the Temple service. His gloss compares Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon, while Hyman’s condensed citation mentions Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah. Hyman’s chronological objection to the Epistle remains his argument.

The linked Shabbat has bar Dasai, Bava Batra has ben Dosai, Makkot has bar Dasi, and Sanhedrin 4:1 has bar Dasayi. In Sanhedrin 2:1 the Gemara then discusses Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah, while Pnei Moshe explains the point of interruption with reference to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon. Hyman’s objection to the chronology in the Epistle remains his argument.
